decisions: The extension implementation belongs in the repository root, not under zandbox.
Zed-native primitives will be used: extension.toml, Rust/WASM, slash commands, context server, and .zed tasks.
The runtime sidecar is Node ESM with zero external dependencies so it can run even before npm installs or Rust setup.
The Rust extension uses a local path dependency on zed-editor/crates/extension_api for workspace-local development.
The example config avoids embedded secrets and uses passwordEnv placeholders.
issues: Rust toolchain is not installed in the current environment, so cargo build and actual dev-extension compilation were not executed.
The MCP sidecar logic exists, but end-to-end validation inside Zed still needs to be done manually after Rust is available and the dev extension is installed.
next_steps: Install rustup and cargo, then add the wasm32-wasip2 target.
Run npm run build:wasm from the repository root.
Install the repository root as a Zed dev extension and verify slash commands plus the database-client context server.
Start replacing the scaffold-only db_run_query path with real PostgreSQL and MySQL adapters.
